holidays.name: National Pig Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble pig, one of the smartest and most underrated barnyard animals. Fans honor pigs with pink decorations, pig-themed snacks (bacon optional, though a bit awkward), and plenty of oinking.
holidays.origin: Created in 1972 by sisters Ellen Stanley, a teacher from Lubbock, Texas, and Mary Lynne Rave of North Carolina, who wanted pigs to be recognized as intelligent, clever companions and not just farm animals.
holidays.funFact: Pigs are often ranked among the smartest animals on Earth, and they can learn to play simple video games with a joystick, sometimes outperforming certain primates.

holidays.name: National Peanut Butter Lover's Day
holidays.description: A sticky, nutty celebration of everyone's favorite pantry staple. People mark the day by slathering peanut butter on toast, celery, bananas, and anything else within reach, while the roof of the mouth suffers gloriously.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that grew out of the American love for peanut butter, which became a household staple in the early 20th century and was a favorite of soldiers during World War II.
holidays.funFact: It takes about 540 peanuts to make a single 12-ounce jar of peanut butter, and under U.S. rules, anything labeled peanut butter must contain at least 90 percent peanuts.

holidays.name: National Horse Protection Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to raising awareness about horse welfare, neglect, and the importance of protecting these majestic animals. Supporters donate, volunteer at rescues, and give a few well-deserved carrots.
holidays.origin: Founded in 2005 by animal welfare advocate and author Colleen Paige, who also launched a number of other animal-related awareness days.
holidays.funFact: Horses can sleep both standing up and lying down, thanks to a special locking mechanism in their legs that lets them doze without falling over.

holidays.name: Zero Discrimination Day
holidays.description: A global day of awareness that encourages people everywhere to embrace diversity, treat each other with respect, and stand up against unfair treatment. It is celebrated with events, campaigns, and the symbol of a butterfly.
holidays.origin: Launched by UNAIDS on March 1, 2014, after the Executive Director Michel Sidibé called for a worldwide movement to end discrimination, especially against people living with HIV.
holidays.funFact: The butterfly was chosen as the symbol of the day because it represents transformation, freedom, and the beauty that comes from change.

holidays.name: Dress in Layers Day
holidays.description: A cheerfully practical holiday that salutes the unpredictable weather of early March, urging everyone to pile on and peel off clothing as the temperature swings between frosty mornings and mild afternoons.
holidays.origin: It is a folk-style observance tied to the changeable weather at the start of meteorological spring in the Northern Hemisphere, popularized through lists of unofficial holidays.
holidays.funFact: Meteorological spring starts on March 1 every year, which is based on the calendar and tidy record-keeping rather than the astronomical equinox that comes about three weeks later.
